qt: to the Commission Arash Saeidi (The Left) Subject:

The unavailability of Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s presidential campaign site on X has raised questions about the risks of foreign interference by digital platforms. This vulnerability also affects international institutions. Judges at the International Criminal Court have been targeted by US sanctions that have led to asset freezes and restrictions on the use of certain financial and digital services. These situations raise questions about the ability of a foreign power to exert pressure, either directly or through its companies, on the European democratic debate or on a judge of an international court. European dependence on foreign technological and financial actors is thus a major challenge for sovereignty and for the protection of democracy. Some countries are seeking to reduce these dependencies: South Korea is developing a national artificial intelligence infrastructure, while France is focusing more on sovereign software solutions (Linux). What urgent action does the Commission plan to take: 1.
to protect European data and our democratic processes from foreign interference?
to ensure our independence and that of international institutions in the face of extraterritorial sanctions?
to put in place a genuine European strategy for strengthening our digital and technological sovereignty?
